content:
The test image shows a soybean field with visible white, cottony/fluffy growth on plant stems and foliage across the canopy, along with yellowing and some plant death. The white mycelial growth is visible on multiple plants throughout the field.

Key observations:
- White, cottony material visible on stems/plant surfaces throughout the field
- Some plants showing yellowing and wilting
- Field-level view showing widespread infection
- No specific leaf spotting pattern visible — the disease appears to affect whole plants

This matches **White Mold** (Sclerotinia sclerotiorum): characteristic white cottony mycelium on aboveground plant parts, with affected plants showing wilting and death. The Frogeye leaf spot reference (which I viewed) shows discrete gray lesions with red-brown margins on individual leaves — clearly different from what's seen here.
